blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Psychology, Humanities & Social Sciences
QUALIFICATION
Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies
Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE)
CAREER LEVEL
Graduate entry
Entry-level analyst or associate, depending on employer

A Consultant helps organisations understand complex problems, evaluate options, and make better decisions. Consultants may work with businesses, government departments, nonprofits, universities, or international organisations.
A PPE degree is particularly useful because it combines three complementary perspectives:

blocks.label: Politics
blocks.text: Understands governments, institutions, public policy, regulation, and power.

blocks.label: Philosophy
blocks.text: Develops logical reasoning, ethical judgement, argument analysis, and critical thinking.

blocks.label: Economics
blocks.text: Builds understanding of markets, incentives, costs, competition, and resource allocation.
Together, these disciplines can prepare graduates for consulting work involving business strategy, public policy, economic research, governance, sustainability, and organisational improvement.
Undergraduate degree
PPE / Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies
Build consulting skills
Research · Excel · Data analysis · Presentations · Case studies
Internship or live project
Consulting firm, corporate strategy team, think tank, NGO, or policy organisation
Entry-level roles
Consulting Analyst · Research Analyst · Strategy Associate · Policy Analyst
Career progression
Progression varies by employer. An MBA or specialist postgraduate degree may help for certain consulting tracks but is not mandatory for every entry-level position.
Year 1
Foundation
Build analytical foundations

items.text: Study introductory economics, political science, philosophy, and social sciences.
Practise structured writing, argument evaluation, and critical reading.
Learn Excel or Google Sheets, basic statistics, and presentation design.
Follow business, economic, and public-policy developments.
Write short analytical reports on real-world problems.

blocks.text: Year 2
Application
Develop consulting methods

items.text: Learn market sizing, problem structuring, root-cause analysis, and hypothesis-driven research.
Study microeconomics, macroeconomics, public finance, and institutional decision-making.
Learn basic data visualisation using Power BI or Tableau.
Conduct surveys, analyse datasets, and prepare evidence-based recommendations.
Participate in debates, case competitions, student consulting clubs, or policy simulations.

blocks.text: Year 3
Specialisation
Build a consulting portfolio

items.text: Choose a consulting focus such as strategy, public policy, economics, or sustainability.
Complete a substantial research paper or applied consulting project.
Pursue internships with consulting firms, corporations, think tanks, NGOs, or government-linked organisations.
Practise case interviews, numerical reasoning, and executive presentations.
Prepare a portfolio with two or three well-documented projects.

blocks.text: Year 4
If applicable
Prepare for recruitment or postgraduate study

items.text: Complete an advanced thesis, capstone, or client-based consulting assignment.
Apply for graduate analyst and associate positions.
Practise consulting interviews and communicate recommendations concisely.
Build professional references and a strong CV.
Decide whether work experience, an MBA, or a specialist master's degree best fits your intended track.

blocks.text: Adapt this plan to the actual duration and curriculum of the selected PPE programme. Some degrees are three years; others offer a four-year honours or research pathway.
A. Strategy and management consulting
Helps organisations solve growth, competition, cost, operating-model, and market-entry problems.

blocks.label: Useful skills
blocks.text: business strategy, financial basics, market research, Excel, case interviews.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: Consulting Analyst, Business Analyst, Strategy Associate.
B. Public policy and governance consulting
Supports policy evaluation, programme design, government initiatives, institutional reform, and impact assessment.

blocks.label: Useful skills
blocks.text: policy research, report writing, stakeholder analysis, statistics, economics.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: Policy Analyst, Governance Consultant, Programme Analyst.
C. Economic and market research consulting
Examines market conditions, consumer behaviour, industry trends, pricing, competition, and economic outcomes.

blocks.label: Useful skills
blocks.text: statistics, economic modelling, research methods, Excel, data visualisation.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: Economic Research Analyst, Market Intelligence Analyst, Research Consultant.
D. ESG, sustainability and social-impact consulting
Helps organisations assess environmental, social, governance, and development challenges.

blocks.label: Useful skills
blocks.text: impact measurement, sustainability frameworks, stakeholder engagement, research.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: ESG Analyst, Sustainability Consultant, Social Impact Analyst.

rows.text: Issue trees, root-cause analysis, hypothesis testing
Literature reviews, source evaluation, surveys, interviews
Percentages, ratios, descriptive statistics, basic economics
Industry structure, business models, costs, revenue
Conflicts of interest, fairness, evidence integrity

blocks.text: Data and productivity
Excel or Google Sheets, PowerPoint or Google Slides, and Word or Google Docs.
Analysis and visualisation
Power BI or Tableau; basic SQL or Python can be useful for data-heavy consulting roles.
Research
Google Scholar, government statistical publications, central bank reports, industry reports, and credible academic databases.
AI-assisted work
Use AI tools to brainstorm hypotheses, organise research, and improve drafts. Verify evidence independently and never upload confidential client data to unauthorised tools.
Aim to complete at least three projects that demonstrate different consulting skills.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Business growth strategy

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Strategy consulting
Select a small business and investigate a problem such as declining sales, customer retention, or expansion into a new market.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Problem statement, competitor analysis, spreadsheet-based findings, three prioritised recommendations, and a 10-slide presentation.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Public-policy evaluation

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Policy consulting
Examine a public programme using publicly available data. Define the intended outcomes and assess what the available evidence does—and does not—show.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Policy brief, evidence table, stakeholder map, limitations, and practical recommendations.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Market-entry analysis

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Economic and market research
Evaluate whether a hypothetical company should enter a selected Indian market or city.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Market sizing assumptions, customer segments, competitor comparison, risks, and a go/no-go recommendation.
For each project, explain the question, method, evidence, limitations, recommendation, and expected impact. Clearly label hypothetical data and avoid presenting estimated results as verified facts.

How to become internship-ready

items.text: Create a one-page CV highlighting research, analytical writing, leadership, and quantitative skills.
Complete two or three portfolio projects.
Practise market-sizing exercises and structured case questions.
Learn to explain your recommendations in a concise, evidence-based way.
Apply to relevant openings and seek referrals from alumni, faculty, and professional contacts.

blocks.text: Certifications can strengthen your profile, but they do not replace project work, analytical ability, or interview preparation.

rows.text: Case-interview preparation and business problem-solving courses
Introductory statistics, data visualisation, and Power BI or Tableau
Microeconomics, macroeconomics, and applied econometrics foundations
Policy analysis, monitoring and evaluation, and impact assessment
Business writing, presentation design, and structured storytelling

blocks.text: Choose courses from reputable universities, professional bodies, or established learning platforms. Check the syllabus, assessment method, and cost before enrolling.
A postgraduate degree can be useful when the target role requires deeper specialisation or when it supports advancement.
MBA or master's in management
Best aligned with management consulting, corporate strategy, operations, and business leadership. Admission and recruiting requirements vary by institution.
Master's in Public Policy or Public Administration
Suitable for governance, public-sector advisory, policy evaluation, and development consulting.
Master's in Economics or Applied Economics
Useful for economic consulting, market analysis, competition-related research, and quantitative policy work. Check mathematics and statistics prerequisites.
Master's in International Relations or Development Studies
Appropriate for international development, geopolitical risk, programme evaluation, and global-policy advisory.
Consultants may work in:

items.text: Management and strategy consulting firms
Corporate strategy, transformation, and business operations teams
Economic research and market intelligence firms
Public-policy think tanks and research institutes
Nonprofits and development organisations
Sustainability and ESG advisory teams
Government advisory and programme implementation projects

blocks.text: The type of work, recruitment process, and degree requirements vary significantly across these environments.

rows.text: Research, data analysis, benchmarking, presentation preparation
Own workstreams, analyse findings, develop recommendations
Lead project modules, coordinate teams, manage client interactions
Manage delivery, timelines, quality, and client relationships
Lead accounts, develop business, oversee major engagements

blocks.text: Progression is performance-based and varies by firm. Some organisations use different titles or career tracks.
Use this checklist to assess readiness for entry-level consulting roles.
Readiness tracker
I can structure an unfamiliar problem into smaller questions.
I can analyse data in Excel or Google Sheets.
I can write a concise, evidence-based report.
I can present recommendations in a clear slide deck.
I understand basic economics and business models.
I have completed at least two relevant portfolio projects.
I have completed an internship, client project, or substantial research assignment.
I have practised case interviews and numerical reasoning.
My CV demonstrates measurable contributions and analytical work.
Complete the items as you build your consulting profile. This is a self-assessment, not a hiring guarantee.
By graduation, a strong candidate for consulting roles should be able to:

items.text: Apply PPE concepts to real business, economic, and public-policy problems.
Research complex issues and evaluate evidence critically.
Analyse quantitative information and communicate findings accurately.
Develop practical recommendations while acknowledging risks and limitations.
Present work professionally to clients, managers, or research teams.
Demonstrate these capabilities through projects, internships, or research experience.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Target Consulting Analyst, Business Analyst, or Research Analyst roles, then specialise based on whether you most enjoy business strategy, economics, public policy, or social-impact work.
